title: Zero-Touch Network Readiness Assistant + Risk‑SLA Calculator for Private Deploy Intake
creator: Rohan Singh
description: Problem: Enterprise customers frequently submit private/VPC/on-prem requests with incomplete network context: intermittent egress windows, restrictive proxy policies, and outdated upgrade maintenance windows. This creates high engineering touch and long lead times. Opportunity: build a zero-touch front-door assistant that performs an automated quick-score and produces a deterministic set of engagement lanes (Self-serve, Concierge, Fast-Track, Blocker) plus a calculated SLA credit and remediation checklist to surface expected effort to sales/CS and engineering.
acceptance_criteria: Assistant returns a Network Maturity Index (NMI) score for a customer based on five lightweight inputs in < 3 minutes
Outputs a recommended engagement lane (Self-serve | Concierge | Fast-Track | Blocker) with rationale and top 5 remediation steps
Generates an estimated engineering effort bucket (Hours: Low/Medium/High) and proposed SLA credit percentage when SLA exceptions are requested
Includes a downloadable preflight bundle (probe script, expected port list, sample firewall rules) tailored to the customer’s environment
Integrates with intake form and creates a prepopulated Linear PM ticket with NMI, lane, remediation steps, and suggested assignees
comments: 2026-01-20: Kickoff — aligned with Sales, Solutions, and Eng on scope; prioritized quick-score and lane mapping. Action: Eng to prototype probe script, Solutions to draft intake questions.
2026-02-02: Design review — added explicit egress window subscore and proxy-complexity multiplier after Solutions provided 6 customer examples where ephemeral egress required special handling.

2026-02-18: Engineering spike completed — lightweight probe collects port reachability, DNS resolution, and outbound TLS handshake timing. Prototype results show 92% detection rate for egress-window inconsistencies in testbed.

2026-02-25: PM and Sales agreed on SLA credit model (see description) but requested a conservative default to avoid overpromising. Action: set Fast-Track cap at 10% SLA credit and require Exec signoff for anything higher.

2026-03-05: In-progress — preparing integration spec for intake form and Linear ticket auto-generation. Blocker: need legal sign-off on collected telemetry terms for automated probes in air-gapped environments. Assigned to Legal intake (pending).
detailed_notes:
Design decisions and algorithm: We create a compact Network Maturity Index (NMI) to drive deterministic lanes. NMI inputs (all scored 0-100): connectivity_score (active probe reachability across canonical egress endpoints), egress_window_score (length and predictability of maintenance windows), proxy_complexity (presence of TLS inspection, client certs, nonstandard proxy chains), routing_surface (NAT, double-NAT, multi-region), and security_policy_strictness (approved egress domains, DLP, deep packet inspection). NMI = round(0.35*connectivity_score + 0.25*egress_window_score + 0.20*(100 - proxy_complexity) + 0.10*(100 - routing_surface) + 0.10*(100 - security_policy_strictness)).

Engagement lanes by NMI: NMI >= 80 -> Self-serve (automated instructions + preflight bundle); 60-79 -> Concierge (Solutions-led 1 call + probe validation); 40-59 -> Fast-Track (engineer-assisted preflight + scheduled ephemeral egress window); <40 -> Blocker (requires remediation before deployment). Each lane includes a default engineering effort bucket mapping (Self-serve: Low <8h; Concierge: Medium 8-24h; Fast-Track: High 24-80h; Blocker: >80h).

SLA credit calculator: When customers need a lower-latency SLA or guaranteed upgrade runway outside standard windows we compute a recommended credit percentage as: Credit = min(10%, base * (1 - NMI/100)) where base = 0.15 if customer requests same-day upgrades, base = 0.10 for <48h maintenance windows. This produces conservative credits that scale down with higher NMI. Sales can override with Exec approval.

Preflight bundle: generated per customer and includes a short shell probe (non-invasive), templated firewall rules, recommended proxy bypass endpoints, expected port list, a remediation playbook (top-5 fixes), and a JSON manifest suitable for uploading to our console telemetry. For air-gapped customers the assistant produces an offline ZIP with instructions for manual execution and a short questionnaire to capture the output for analyst ingestion.

Telemetry and privacy: Probe defaults to collecting only reachability, latency, and TLS handshake timings, never payload. For air-gapped/manual probes we require explicit customer consent and an intake checkbox. Legal must sign off before we distribute probe artifacts for any customer run.

Instrumentation: Outputs are stored as structured fields attached to the intake ticket: nmi_score, recommended_lane, estimated_hours_bucket, sla_credit_pct, remediation_list (comma-separated). These fields drive downstream automation (ticket routing to Concierge team or auto-assign to on-call engineer).

Tradeoffs: A lightweight automated probe minimizes sales friction but cannot detect deeply nested proxy policies or corporate DLP. We accept increased False Negative risk for proxy complexity and plan a low-friction escalator flow to Concierge when probe confidence is low.

Next steps: 1) Legal review for probe distribution (blocker). 2) Engineering to harden probe and add offline ZIP generator (due 2026-03-22). 3) Integrate result fields into intake form and implement Linear auto-create (due 2026-03-29). 4) Pilot with two high-fit customers (target windows 2026-04).
